spatial_claims.claim: Lines a and b are medial straight lines with a > b; rectangle R = a*b is medial
Third proportional c satisfies a:b = b:c, so ac = b²; magnitude ordering a > b > c
Segments a and c are adjoined end-to-end on a straight line forming segment of length a+c
The segment a+c is bisected at its midpoint; d = (a+c)/2 is the half-length, e = (a-c)/2 is the offset from midpoint to division point
Proposition 2.5 applied to segment a+c cut equally at midpoint and unequally at junction of a and c, giving ac + e² = d²

configuration_map: The construction is entirely one-dimensional. Segments a and c are placed end-to-end on a single straight line, forming a segment of total length a+c. The midpoint of this segment defines d = (a+c)/2. The junction between a and c is offset from the midpoint by e = (a-c)/2 (positive since a > c). Proposition 2.5 is applied to this linear configuration to derive d² = b² + e². All subsequent reasoning (Steps 5-7) is purely algebraic, manipulating commensurability relations among magnitudes d, b, a, e, and areas. No two-dimensional spatial configuration (triangles, circles, angles, interior/exterior relations) is constructed or invoked.
pass_reason: The proof is primarily algebraic/proportional, dealing with commensurability of medial magnitudes. The only geometric construction is a trivial one-dimensional segment arrangement (adjoin two segments, bisect the result) used to invoke Prop. 2.5 for an algebraic identity. All linear spatial claims are mutually consistent. No angle decompositions, triangle interior/exterior arguments, or complex 2D/3D configurations are present, so there is no possibility of spatial contradiction.
